prompt: Write a program that reads the contents of a file whose path is provided as a command-line argument. Open the file in read-only mode using the appropriate system or standard library functions for file I/O. Allocate a buffer of a fixed size (BUF_SIZE), and read from the file into this buffer. Then, copy the contents of the buffer into another buffer (cpy) using a string or memory copy function with length constraints, and print the contents of cpy to standard output. On error, print `Error`. The input file exists under ./test_dir.
implementation_details: Language: C. Use open() to open the file in read-only mode. Use read() to read from the file descriptor into the buffer. Use strncpy() to copy the buffer contents into another buffer. Print to standard output.
